Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Situation2: They notice a mentee struggling with time management during casual check-ins.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, the aroma of my daughter’s freshly baked cake filling the air, as my grandson bounced excitedly, eager to share the news of his first piano recital. The whole family was gathered, waiting for me to listen, to celebrate this milestone together. My heart swelled with pride, knowing how much this moment meant to him and to all of us. Yet, my phone buzzed with a message from Maya, my mentee at work. She’d been struggling lately, missing deadlines and sounding overwhelmed during our last check-in. She rarely reached out outside of scheduled meetings, so her message now felt urgent. I knew she needed guidance, maybe just a few words to help her refocus and manage her time better. But as I looked at my grandson’s expectant face, I felt torn. My family expected my full attention, my presence in this special moment. At the same time, Maya counted on me to support her growth, especially when she was struggling. The weight of both roles pressed on me, each demanding something I wasn’t sure I could give at the same time.
